item.description: Wednesday, October 7, 2026 | Memphis Listening Lab | 7 PM | WYXR Presents
item.content:encoded:
📻 WYXR Presents

Dave Schools w/Colin Butler

Memphis Listening Lab

Wednesday, October 7, 2026

Time: 7 PM

Before joining Widespread Panic onstage at MEMPHO Fest, bassist Dave Schools is making time for an intimate hang with Memphis fans at Memphis Listening Lab. Join Schools on Wednesday, Oct. 7, as he steps behind the turntables to spin records, talk music, and spend an evening with fellow music lovers. He’ll be joined by Memphis musician and DJ Colin Butler of Big Ass Truck and WYXR’s “Courtesy Flush Sound System” for this special one-hour session presented by WYXR and Memphis Listening Lab. The event begins at 7 p.m., with doors opening at 6:30 p.m. Admission is free with RSVP, but space is limited. It will be broadcast live on WYXR.org and 91.7 FM in Memphis.

item.title: The Cramps "Greatest Gravy" Listen Up Session w/Henry Rollins (SOLD OUT) — Memphis Listening Lab
item.description: Saturday, October 10, 2026 | Memphis Listening Lab | 6:00-7:30pm | WYXR Presents
item.content:encoded:
📻 WYXR Presents

The Cramps "Greatest Gravy" Listen Up Session w/Henry Rollins (SOLD OUT)

Memphis Listening Lab

Saturday, October 10, 2026

Time: 6:00-7:30pm

1977 Alex Chilton convinced The Cramps to come to Memphis and record at Ardent. Those sessions gave us their first two singles, but there was a lot more on the tapes. Now, almost 50 years later, Gravest Gravy finally brings those recordings out. Henry Rollins was directly involved in going through the surviving mixes and choosing the versions that made the record, and on October 10 he’s coming to MLL to play it for us and talk about how it all happened. Henry is also bringing a test pressing with alternate mixes from Songs the Lord Taught Us. He suggested a little homework before the event: give the regular version of the record a listen. It’s about 35 minutes and you’ll be able to hear what’s different when he plays the alternate mixes. Not required, obviously, but we like the idea. The Cramps. Ardent. Alex Chilton. A record almost 50 years in the making, coming back to Memphis. We’re pretty excited about this. This event is part of MLL's Listen Up series and is free, but seating is extremely limited and an RSVP is required. CURRENTLY SOLD OUT!

item.title: Memphis Drone (12+ artists) — H and S Printing Company
item.description: Monday, October 19, 2026 | H and S Printing Company | 6 PM | WYXR Pick
item.content:encoded:
⭐ WYXR Pick

Memphis Drone (12+ artists)

H and S Printing Company

Monday, October 19, 2026

Time: 6 PM

NASHVILLE, TN – September 22, 2026 – chatterbird, a Nashville-based chamber ensemble, is excited to partner with Memphis Print Shop and numerous Memphis-based artists for Memphis Drone, a six-hour concert of uninterrupted sound. The concert takes place at Memphis Print Shop on Monday, October 19, from 6:00 PM until midnight. Memphis Drone is co-produced by Jenny Davis, Robert Traxler, Unmanageable Arts, Hyasynth House, and Gezellig Records. Tickets are on sale now and can be purchased here. Memphis Drone is part of three durational drone concerts across Tennessee, with the other two taking place at future dates and locations later this fall. Each six-hour concert featuring over twelve musicians performing interlocking, collaborative sets will transform communities into temporary creative ecosystems where musicians, visual artists, and audiences explore sustained sound and shifting tones over time. Featured performers for Memphis Drone include chatterbird, Dwight Van de Vate, Eudamonia Flue Quartet, Eve Maret, Infinity Stairs, Madame Fraankie, Marcella Simien, Optic Sink, Robby Grant, Sean Murphy, Tamar Love, and Thomas Corbin. Designed as miniature community festivals, these experimental durational concerts, often called “drones”, prioritize deep listening, presence, improvisation, collaboration, and collective participation. Defined by sustained tones and repetition, drone is one of the world’s oldest musical forms, resonating across cultures from Indigenous Australian didgeridoos and Indian tanpuras to Scottish bagpipes and Tibetan Buddhist chant. By centering this universal musical structure, the project creates an accessible framework for participation while uplifting artists who work outside commercial music systems. ABOUT THE PRODUCERS: JENNY DAVIS is a Memphis-based musician, arts administrator, and community arts organizer. A flutist by training, she has worked across performance, music education, and nonprofit arts leadership. She is interested in creating collaborative, accessible arts experiences that bring together artists, organizations, and audiences through experiences that encourage connection, curiosity, and collaboration. ROBERT TRAXLER started the Memphis Concrète experimental electronic music festival in 2017. He sometimes makes his own music. CHATTERBIRD is a chamber music ensemble that explores alternative instrumentation, stylistic diversity, and interdisciplinary collaboration in order to create thoughtful, intimate, and inventive musical experiences. Formed in 2014, chatterbird performs classical music that skirts traditional boundaries, sliding between classical, jazz, hip-hop, rock, avant-garde, and country, creating a thoughtful and inventive way to discover and experience modern classical music. HYASYNTH HOUSE was founded in 2018 and is a Nashville-based electronic music collective that serves to empower female and LQBTQIA+ artists in the community through the curation of public workshops, showcases, and live music performances. IG: @hyasynth_house GEZELLIG ARTS is the live event services branch of Gezellig Records, an internationally-minded/Knoxville-based independent record label run by Ben Smith, who also organized the 12-Hour Drone events as part of the 2018 + 2019 editions of the Big Ears Festival. UNMANAGEABLE ARTS is a 501c3 non-profit whose mission is to mobilize resources and build power for artists engaged in social change work. We support artist-driven projects that connect across history, culture, and communities, and prioritize projects that are anti-racist and rooted in feminist ideology.

item.title: The Robert Cray Band — Germantown Performing Arts Center
item.description: Saturday, October 24, 2026 | Germantown Performing Arts Center | 8:00 PM | WYXR Pick
item.content:encoded:
⭐ WYXR Pick

The Robert Cray Band

Germantown Performing Arts Center

Saturday, October 24, 2026

Time: 8:00 PM

Blues icon. Soul man. Rock and roller. Robert Cray is all these things—and more. Born in Georgia and raised in Washington, the musician first picked up a guitar after seeing The Beatles on TV. When he witnessed Jimi Hendrix perform in Seattle, he determined that his destiny would follow a similar path, and so it has. Over the past 50 years, Robert Cray has developed into one of American music’s most singular artists. Robert Cray’s story is one of struggle and commitment—struggle and commitment that have led to phenomenal success. He has sold millions of albums and countless concert tickets, won five Grammy Awards, been inducted into the Blues Hall of Fame, received an Americana Music Lifetime Achievement Award, and designed two signature model Fender guitars. Yet for Robert, what’s always mattered most is the music. Every note he plays counts, and every song he sings is delivered as if it is his last. Integrity and intensity are what have guided Cray’s musical career, and he has never cheapened his output or delivered a substandard performance. Indeed, his commitment to making music of the highest standard has won Cray both a loyal audience and the respect of many of popular music’s most legendary figures. Robert Cray has shared the stage and/or studio with the likes of John Lee Hooker, Muddy Waters, B.B. King, Buddy Guy, Chuck Berry, Albert Collins, The Rolling Stones, Eric Clapton, Tina Turner, Stevie Ray Vaughan, the Memphis Horns, and the Hi Rhythm Section. Cray’s stinging guitar playing and soulful voice as well as his skills as a band leader and a performer mark him as a keeper of the flame for American roots music and an artist who never fails to deliver. We are thrilled to present the Robert Cray Band in the intimate setting of the Highland Capital Performance Hall on Saturday, October 24, at 8:00 PM. Don’t miss your chance to see this music legend!

item.title: WYXR's Raised By Sound Fest - Soccer Mommy w/Late Night Cardigan — Satellite Music Hall
item.description: Friday, December 4, 2026 | Satellite Music Hall | 7 PM | WYXR Presents
item.content:encoded:
📻 WYXR Presents

WYXR's Raised By Sound Fest - Soccer Mommy w/Late Night Cardigan

Satellite Music Hall

Friday, December 4, 2026

Time: 7 PM

Soccer Mommy Dubbed by Rolling Stone as “one of Indie Rock’s most beloved singer-songwriters,” Swiss-born and Nashville-based Soccer Mommy (Sophie Allison) has built a loyal following with her plaintive, confessional storytelling suffused with indie pop/rock sensibilities. WYXR is elated to have her headline the first Friday night Raised By Sound Fest show. Late Night Cardigan For those who love biting lyrics and soaring power-pop anthems, Late Night Cardigan is Memphis’ worst kept secret. WYXR has been a fan for years, and you will be too. Look for a new album this fall “One Million Dollars” then catch them on the big stage at the brand new Satellite Music Hall in support of Soccer Mommy and WYXR. WYXR’s Raised By Sound Fest celebrates Memphis music, new and old, across multiple genres and features our unique group of volunteer DJs. It will feature free, day-long performances on Saturday, a ticketed headline concert on Friday, and a ticketed headline concert and after-party on Saturday night.

item.title: WYXR's Raised By Sound Fest - Wednesday, Patterson Hood, Sylvan Esso DJ Set, Hand Habits, Chanel Beads and more! — Crosstown Arts
item.description: Saturday, December 5, 2026 | Crosstown Arts | 1p | WYXR Presents
item.content:encoded:
📻 WYXR Presents

WYXR's Raised By Sound Fest - Wednesday, Patterson Hood, Sylvan Esso DJ Set, Hand Habits, Chanel Beads and more!

Crosstown Arts

Saturday, December 5, 2026

Time: 1p

Wednesday (solo) + Patterson Hood Two Southern storytelling powerhouses join forces for an intimate set to raise funds for WYXR. It’s only fitting that they co-headline the station’s biggest fundraiser since they’re the embodiment of the independent and unconventional spirit of WYXR. This will be the first full show featuring Karly Hartzman (Wednesday) and Patterson Hood (Drive-By Truckers) and it’s sure to be heavy on the Memphis love (they’ve performed Big Star and Chris Bell tunes live) and light on the formality. Don’t miss it. East Atrium Sylvan Esso DJ Set Saturday, Dec. 5 Doors 8:30 pm – Show 9 – 11 pm You might know Sylvan Esso (Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn) by their catchy, electro-pop tunes, most recently their incredible new album Ow ∞. The two have also been making waves as a DJ duo with discerning Reddit users describing their DJ sets as “nonstop, absolute riots” and “great bangers back to back.” This will be their first performance in Memphis in what’s quickly become a can’t-miss, fan favorite at the fest. Your after-party ticket gets you complimentary food by Go-Time Group (Fawn, Cameo, Mary’s B.O.T.E., No Comment), wine, beer, cocktails, art experiences and more. Your VIP ticket to Saturday’s headline show of Wednesday (solo) and Patterson Hood includes after party access. Central & East Atrium Spend the day at Raised By Sound Fest for free live music from 1 to 6:30 pm along with community tables featuring local organizations lifting up the arts, animal rescue, music and much more. Family and dog friendly! 5:15 pm Central Atrium Chanel Beads An experimental dream pop project by New York-based Shane Levers, Chanel Beads makes their first appearance in Memphis at Raised By Sound Fest. Their June 2026 sophomore album, Your Day Will Come (same title as their first album), earned praise from renowned Indie Music staples NME, Pitchfork and Paste. 3:55 pm East Atrium Hand Habits WYXR is elated to present the Memphis debut of Hand Habits, aka Meg Duffy. Their contributions to collaboration and community in the Indie music world are right in line with WYXR. Along with their incredible solo project, Hand Habits, they’ve brought their immense swiss-army-like talents (vocals, keys, bass, guitar, slide) and vision to work by Kevin Morby, The War on Drugs, Perfume Genius, and more. 2:50 pm East Atrium Out On The Eaves The current creative venture by Memphis mainstay, Patrick Carey, is a stunning display of psychedelic folk and pop. Patrick cut his teeth in Athens, Georgia, but since landing in Memphis, has become embedded in the local arts scene and has released two exceptional albums as Out On The Eaves. His 2026 release, With No Reflection, is a revelation and was launched at a release party with none other than Bonnie “Prince” Billy. 2 pm Central Atrium Marcella Simien + Qemist On their own, Marcella and Qemist are beloved, prolific and ground-breaking Memphis artists. Together, their powers double. Swamp Soul Queen Marcella’s transcendent vocals soar over Qemist’s infectious, perfectly layered beats and melodies. It’s something to behold. This is the first performance of its kind, with visual and stylistic surprises in store. 1 pm Central Atrium Blue Tom Revue The only performance that’s kicked off Raised By Sound Fest since the very beginning. These young artists historically go on to BIG things – including spots at RIVERBEAT and Mempho Fest. It’s your chance to see the future of Memphis music for free – and you can say “I saw them when . . .”
